note: Six of the nine long-standing 'not fixed yet' items. A stubby Von Karman, Haack, parabolic or power-series nose was charged EXACTLY ZERO pressure drag at any fineness, so shortening one made the app predict less drag; it now costs what a wind-tunnel series in Centuri TIR-100 says it costs, fading to nothing by 1.8 calibers so no ordinary nose moves. A rail button now flies the part you typed instead of a generic 9.7 mm one - and saving a .ork no longer writes six hard-coded numbers over the builder's real button. A launch lug, a rail button and a drag bump now sit at the angle you put them at: it never reached the physics engine at all, so every one flew at 180 degrees. A drag bump's drag now varies with speed instead of being frozen at its Mach 0.3 value, and a camera shroud follows the same curve. A shroud sitting in front of a fin now gets a sentence saying the wake it sheds is not modelled. And a RockSim airfoil fin set takes the mass the file states, which is what desktop OpenRocket does - most files get heavier, newer ones much lighter. Mounting angle and drag turns out NOT to be a defect and the note says why.
